overview.text: The arithmetic mean—often called the mean or, in everyday usage, the average—is a measure of a data set’s center, or central tendency. To calculate it, add every value and divide the total by the number of values; each value contributes to the result. The sample mean is commonly written x̄, while the mean of an entire population is written μ. The mean gives a single summary of a data set, but it may not describe a typical value well: unusually high or low values can pull it away from where most observations lie. When outliers are present, the median may better represent the center.

key_facts.text: Formula: arithmetic mean = sum of all data values ÷ number of values.
The sample mean is denoted x̄ (“x-bar”); the population mean is denoted μ.
If values repeat, you can multiply each distinct value by how often it occurs, add those products, and divide by the total number of values.
The mean is a measure of center, alongside other measures such as the median and mode.
Outliers can strongly affect the mean; the median is less sensitive to them and may be a better summary when extreme values are present.
